title: How long does the local train take for the whole journey?
description: A local train stops at three stations at equal distances, taking t minutes between stations and stopping two minutes at each. A rough diagram gives the time for t equal to four and the expression for any t.
teaching_notes: One idea: three stops between the two ends make four equal journeys, and the stops add separately. Watch for students who use three journeys instead of four.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of counting each kind separately and adding: the travel time and the stopping time are written separately and added.
video_script.substitution: The method of counting horizontal and diagonal matchsticks separately and adding, with the travel time and the stopping time in place of the matchsticks.
video_script.anchor: a rough diagram of a train line with the two end places and three stations between them
video_script.payoff_line: The journey takes twenty two minutes when t is four, and four t plus six minutes in all

final_answer.spoken: twenty two minutes when t is four, and four t plus six minutes in all

never_show: the finished total before the answer beat
maths_rules: three stations between the two end places make 4 equal journeys
video_script.design: One idea: the journeys and the stops are counted separately and then added. Assumes the example of counting each kind and adding. A rough diagram of the line with the stations stays on the stage.
open_questions: The book names the two end places; the video says the two end places, since neither is a character with a name slot.

marks.p1: the title card From your book arrives

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>A local train goes from one place to another, stopping at three stations on the way. The stations are at equal distances.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>It takes t minutes to go from one station to the next. It stops for two minutes at each of the three stations.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>What is the time for the whole journey, and what is it if t is four?

beats.on_screen: the train line stays on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a rough diagram: two end places and three stations in a line ; the gaps between neighbours are the journeys

marks.g1: a line with two end places and three stations in between is drawn
marks.g2: a curved arrow is drawn over each gap between neighbours

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Draw a rough line with the two end places and the three stations between them.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Each gap between two neighbours on the line is one journey.

beats.on_screen: Given: 3 stations at equal distances ; t minutes from one station to the next ; 2 minutes stop at each station

marks.gv1: 3 stations and t minutes are written
marks.gv2: 2 minutes at each station is written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, there are three stations, and each journey from one station to the next takes t minutes.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>The train stops for two minutes at each station.

beats.on_screen: To find: (a) the time for t = 4 ; (b) the expression for the time
narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We find the time for t equal to four, and then the expression for any t. We work the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 3 stations between the two ends make 4 equal journeys, so travel time = 4 × t = 4t

marks.s1a: the four gaps on the diagram are numbered

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, count the journeys on the diagram. Three stations between the two end places make four gaps.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Each journey takes t minutes, so the travel time is four times t, which is four t minutes.
<bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, count the stops. The train stops at three stations for two minutes each, which is six minutes.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: total = 4t + 6 minutes ; (a) with t = 4: 4 × 4 + 6 = 16 + 6 = 22 minutes

marks.s3a: the travel time and the stopping time are added

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, add the travel time and the stopping time. The expression is four t plus six minutes.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>For t equal to four, we get four times four plus six. That is sixteen plus six, which is twenty two minutes.

marks.s4b: the four journeys and three stops are added one by one on the diagram

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Fourth, check with t as five. The expression gives four times five plus six, which is twenty six minutes.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>On the diagram, four journeys of five and three stops of two add to twenty six as well.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The journey takes twenty two minutes when t is four, and four t plus six minutes in all.
